sourceFacts.fact: A focal seizure begins in a network limited to one hemisphere and can spread to involve both sides.
Network recruitment is a functional concept; a simplified node diagram does not show cortical topography or actual pathways.

layoutSpecification: Title 'Focal seizure: possible network spread'. Two identical ABSTRACT networks side-by-side on plain ivory background, with no head, brain, organ outlines, hemispheres, cortical contours, neural tracts or body parts. Each network is exactly NINE equally spaced circular nodes in a simple 3-by-3 grid connected by faint straight horizontal and vertical grey lines. LEFT heading 'Limited onset': only the TOP-LEFT and TOP-CENTRE nodes are ochre; all other seven nodes are pale teal. RIGHT heading 'Wider recruitment': seven of the nine nodes are ochre, with the original two still ochre, and two bottom-corner nodes remain pale teal. A single broad arrow BETWEEN the two grids labelled 'May spread'. Bottom 'Abstract network • not brain anatomy'. This is a conceptual increase in recruited network, not a physical tract map or a claim that spread always happens. No EEG. CRITICAL readability: fully OPAQUE near-white/ivory background across the entire canvas. NO black, dark-blue or dark gradient background; NO transparency, vignette, neon glow, coloured halos, blur or shadow fields. ALL lettering solid deep navy, plainly readable at small size against near-white. Flat pastel nodes, thin grey connections and one rightward arrow only. Exact two 3x3 grids and the counts already specified.
forbiddenAnatomy: No internal organ, eye, ear, brain, tissue or bone anatomy
No diagnostic image, patient-specific lesion appearance or literal anatomical pathway
